keep_features.feature_value: Very informal, emphatic personal testimony ("I love America" / "It is great")
keep_features.evidence_span: "I think America is great and always has been, I love America"
keep_features.rationale: First-person praise is expressed in a casual, conversational register with repetitive emphasis.

keep_features.feature_value: All-caps emphasis used for numbers and entities (EMPLOYEES/OWE/IN UNPAID TAXES)
keep_features.rationale: The post uses prominent all-caps formatting to stress claims and figures.

keep_features.feature_value: High density of named actors/institutions (Senator Joni Ernst, IRS, Clinton/Harris referenced in mirror)
keep_features.rationale: Mentions of specific people and organizations are explicit and frequent.

keep_features.feature_value: Explicit contrast clause with 'but'/'isn't a design flaw - it's a feature'
keep_features.evidence_span: "but that isn't a design flaw - it's a feature"
keep_features.rationale: Uses a direct contrastive construction to reframe an argument.

keep_features.feature_value: Uses a mass shooting tragedy as evidence of political exploitation and victimization (anti-gun/political grief exploitation)
keep_features.evidence_span: "breaking point... mass shooting in Vegas" / "government use a tragedy to gut the Second Amendment"
keep_features.rationale: The text frames victims/tragedy and political actors as exploiting harm.

keep_features.feature_value: Multiple line breaks/ellipsis and rhetorical punchphrases
keep_features.evidence_span: "Crickets…" / "THEY HAVE ALWAYS BEEN PLAYING US" / "Time to wake up"
keep_features.rationale: Frequent punctuation/ellipsis and exclamatory phrasing increase intensity.

keep_features.feature_value: Direct insult/derogation of politician (small, weak, hypocritical)
keep_features.rationale: The post attacks an actor with pejorative character judgments rather than policy analysis.

keep_features.feature_value: Opposes 'violent criminals' deportation talk to employer attitudes about workers
keep_features.rationale: Contrasts an out-group notion (violent criminals) with an in-group workforce and their perceived treatment.

remove_features.feature_value: Implied rebuttal via generalization/mini-assertion that hot temps don’t mean world ending
remove_features.evidence_span: "a hot summer does NOT mean the world is ending"
remove_features.rationale: States a direct claim about interpretation of climate extremes.

remove_features.feature_value: Outgroup vs ingroup: 'MAGAts' vs implied others outside US
remove_features.evidence_span: "MAGAts barely know a world outside the US exists."
remove_features.rationale: Uses a sweeping outgroup characterization tied to geographic limitation.

remove_features.evidence_span: "his sheep will continue to follow daddy trump"
remove_features.rationale: Uses ridicule through 'sheep' metaphor and parental nicknaming.
Employs a politically charged slur-like label for the target group.

remove_features.feature_value: Judgmental, moralized condemnation and celebration ("dick move", "narcissistic blight")
remove_features.rationale: Uses moral/emotive condemnation terms to evaluate political behavior.

remove_features.feature_value: Empirical-sounding contrast using lived experience and state-by-state claims
remove_features.evidence_span: "Every blue state has a ton of firearm regulation... I've actually lived in them."
remove_features.rationale: Presents concrete factual comparisons and personal experience as support.

remove_features.feature_value: Implied direct action/response plan (attend speech then walk out)
remove_features.evidence_span: "getting up and walking out when he spouts something stupid."
remove_features.rationale: Communicates an intended behavioral response to political speech content.

remove_features.feature_value: Cumulative attributive characterization with multiple descriptors
remove_features.evidence_span: "abandoned conservative principles and merely Trump’s plaything and swampier than the one he claimed he was going to drain"
remove_features.rationale: Stacks multiple related negative predicates connected by 'and' for emphasis.
